issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String (SealSaloon(String)) for the saloon name, but both the provided template usage and the reference solution use a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signature and whether a name field must be stored.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to specify a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) if no name is needed, or (B) change the template Main and the solution SealSaloon to provide and use a constructor SealSaloon(String name) and add a corresponding private name field and getter. Alternatively, support both by adding an overloaded no-arg constructor and a SealSaloon(String) constructor so both usages are valid.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String (SealSaloon(String)) for the saloon name, but both the template usage and the provided solution use a parameterless constructor (SealSaloon()). This API/signature mismatch prevents students from directly mapping the requirement (constructor with name parameter) to the template/solution implementation and may confuse them about the expected constructor and storing/reading the saloon name.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor API across artifacts. Either update the template and solution to provide a constructor matching the problem statement (public SealSaloon(String name) and store the name with a getter) and update Main to instantiate with a name, or revise the problem statement/UML to specify a parameterless constructor. Prefer implementing public SealSaloon(String name) and adding a private final name field with a getName() method so the code matches the specification.
